milestones.title: See the destination
milestones.why: **See the destination.** Play/watch one reference journey; identify Match, Round, Problem, Run, Submit, Reveal; locate browser, server, storage, and Judge on a simple map. Distinguish reference from practice and team workspaces.
milestones.enables: Know what the game does before creating files.

milestones.title: Set up a practice workspace
milestones.why: **Set up a practice workspace.** Explain root/current directory, editor, terminal, Git status, Node, package manager, package manifest, dependency install, TypeScript tools, and the first run command. Verify versions and each command before proceeding.
milestones.enables: Run one function in your own practice folder.

milestones.title: Move from C to TypeScript and tests
milestones.why: **Move from C to TypeScript and tests.** Functions/parameters/returns; annotations and type erasure; `number` versus C integer types; booleans/strings; objects and arrays; unions, missing values, imports/exports, and basic errors as needed. Explain a test as a function call plus an expected result.
milestones.enables: Test a boundary and explain a changed case.

milestones.title: Represent the game and change its state
milestones.why: **Represent the game and change its state.** Player/side IDs, Match/Round records, allowed phase transitions, membership, injected time, and the difference between a pure decision and a state change. Introduce interfaces as contracts when the first substitute is needed.
milestones.enables: Represent a Match and reject an invalid action.

milestones.title: Give players a Problem and a visible Run
milestones.why: **Give players a Problem and a visible Run.** Problem data and validation; statement/starter languages; separate visible and hidden data; a fake Judge; a Run request and result. Introduce promises/`async`/`await` and error paths around this concrete dependency.
milestones.enables: Run public examples without changing the score.

milestones.title: Submit, evaluate, score, and reveal
milestones.why: **Submit, evaluate, score, and reveal.** Acceptance and pending receipt; request identity and duplicate protection; fake-Judge success/failure; counted scores; normal Reveal; Round resets; summed Match scores and tie-breaks; Match deadline and bounded reveal grace. Teach these as separate slices.
milestones.enables: Finish a local Match with tested scoring and deadlines.

milestones.title: Expose a small server API
milestones.why: **Expose a small server API.** Process/port; HTTP request/response; JSON; route/controller/service; runtime input validation; trusted identity seam; status/error responses. Explain the reference framework's modules and dependency injection only as the small route needs them.
milestones.enables: Call your rules through a small server API.

milestones.title: Build the screen around working behavior
milestones.why: **Build the screen around working behavior.** HTML/CSS and browser events; then TypeScript components, props/state, rendering, effects/cleanup, forms, editor integration, and requests. Begin with one input/button/result; expand to Problem/editor/Run/Submit/Reveal/final result. Introduce a transport interface when separating the screen from the connection.
milestones.enables: Use one browser to play through your local game.

milestones.title: Save and recover the game
milestones.why: **Save and recover the game.** Memory store versus database; schema/relations and JSONB where used; persistence interface and Postgres adapter; transactions/revisions; durable evaluation ownership; work outside short locks; restart and failed-write recovery; publish events only after commit.
milestones.enables: Recover saved state and reject stale writes.

milestones.title: Run code through the real Judge boundary
milestones.why: **Run code through the real Judge boundary.** First explain why player programs need isolation. Connect explicit provider selection, worker API, per-case containers, languages, limits, sealed data, queue/readiness, and infrastructure failures. Compare real results with the fake-Judge contract.
milestones.enables: Run player programs through an isolated Judge.

milestones.title: Create a private Lobby and connect two players
milestones.why: **Create a private Lobby and connect two players.** Invite code, side assignment, Ready and host Start; durable Match creation; HTTP versus socket events; trusted socket identity; membership, revisions, first/last-socket presence, stale replies, disconnect/reconnect, and authoritative refresh.
milestones.enables: Invite a second player and recover after reconnect.

milestones.title: Make 2v2 safe and understandable
milestones.why: **Make 2v2 safe and understandable.** Team membership; shared document and revisions; collaboration protocol; round-scoped clients; both-player readiness; readiness invalidation after edits; submission of the agreed document snapshot.
milestones.enables: Keep two teams’ code and readiness separate.

milestones.title: Add Game-owned team chat and client cleanup
milestones.why: **Add Game-owned team chat and client cleanup.** Match scope versus Round scope; chat membership and team isolation; messages/pings; history limits and errors; preservation/disposal of chat and collaboration clients.
milestones.enables: Chat with teammates and clean up old clients.

milestones.title: Integrate, operate, and prove the complete game
milestones.why: **Integrate, operate, and prove the complete game.** Team-repo mapping; real identity/navigation/configuration contracts; Docker/Compose, environment examples, private worker, Nginx/TLS, service readiness, real multiplayer browser journeys, error recovery, README/contributions, and behavior-by-behavior comparison with the reference.
milestones.enables: Check your implementation inside the team app.

lessons.title: Meet the tools before using them
Write a function and run it
Turn a boundary into a test
Move a rule without changing it
Write a changed rule on your own
Map one rule and its test

behaviors.title: Basic rules, state, membership, timing
behaviors.reason: Explain state and reject an action for the correct reason with an injected clock.

behaviors.title: Problems, starter code, visible/hidden separation
behaviors.reason: Render public Problem data and show that hidden inputs remain private.

behaviors.title: Visible Run and failures
behaviors.reason: Run visible cases without changing score; explain compilation/runtime/infrastructure outcomes.

behaviors.title: Submit ownership and acceptance
behaviors.reason: An authorized valid action reaches evaluation; rejected actions do not.

behaviors.title: Evaluation identity, concurrency, failures
behaviors.reason: Replay a same-identity request safely; reject conflicting reuse and avoid duplicate committed outcomes.

behaviors.title: Score, Reveal, Round reset, final result
behaviors.reason: Explain summed scores and tie-breaks; reveal only at the permitted time; reset the appropriate state.

behaviors.title: Match deadline and bounded grace
behaviors.reason: Reject at the exact Match deadline, handle accepted work within grace, and finish durably with unplayed Rounds contributing zero.

behaviors.title: Persistence, revisions, restart
behaviors.reason: Recover durable state and pending work; surface stale writes without silently replaying unsafe commands.

behaviors.title: Post-commit events
behaviors.reason: Failed writes do not publish success; reconnect can recover missed events from authoritative state.

behaviors.title: Execution contract, isolation, provider selection
behaviors.reason: Distinguish fake-Judge logic checks from real execution checks; validate limits and sealing without silently falling back between providers.

behaviors.title: Worker capacity and readiness
behaviors.reason: Explain and check bounded queue, timeout, readiness, and private deployment behavior.

behaviors.title: Invitation Lobby and Match creation
behaviors.reason: Verify host/full-side/Ready rules, concurrent joins/start, stale replies, and one Match handoff.

behaviors.title: Live connection, authorization, presence
behaviors.reason: Reject nonmembers, count multiple sockets correctly, and reconnect without stale-state corruption.

behaviors.title: 2v2 documents and readiness
behaviors.reason: Keep teams isolated, invalidate Ready after edits, and judge the agreed revision.

behaviors.title: Team chat and pings
behaviors.reason: Enforce team membership and explain history limits without claiming durable chat.

behaviors.title: Browser screen and client lifetimes
behaviors.reason: Complete the player journey; show correct deadline-Reveal order; clean up Round-scoped collaboration while preserving Match-scoped chat.

behaviors.title: Runtime/configuration/integration
behaviors.reason: Run the actual target setup with documented prerequisites, ignored secrets, correct identity contracts, and HTTPS/WSS checks.

behaviors.title: Whole-game parity and failure journeys
behaviors.reason: Record target outcomes for complete 1v1/2v2, disconnect/reconnect, failures, and cross-team isolation. Explain meaningful differences.

behaviors.title: Optional/deferred/reference-only code
behaviors.reason: Every item has a reasoned disposition. Optional experiments and service skeletons cannot be presented as production features or silently required builds.
